items.title: Clay Jenkins interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, March 18, 2016
items.q: I knew Fred Sturm who had been the head of the department there.

ctx.x: This could be a hard question, but why — I would assume the position at Eastman, that you have, was a fairly competitive — I mean it’s a respected university throughout the world. So why did they pick you, do you think, as opposed to someone else?

I don’t know. I felt very lucky. I knew a few people there, that didn’t hurt. And I knew Fred Sturm who had been the head of the department there. I really was a fan of Harold Danko’s, who is the piano teacher still there. I had heard him with Thad Jones who was one of my favorites. So when I heard that — they called me. I didn’t know about the job. But I went and interviewed along with four other guys. So I felt pretty good about it. But it was a little bit of a rude awakening once I got there. I wasn’t really…
Organization is a big part of it.
